guard: a first attach against a mesh that is not there is refused in the preflight's classified words, not in the issuer dial's raw transport error
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/workspace build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:attach-reconnect
completionMarker: F. the four classifications the loop turns on
why: The control-caller instrument mint became an issuance, and the issuer session dials the broker
BEFORE the preflight runs. Against a mesh that is not there that dial throws the transport's own
words, which is what cell G of attach-reconnect saw: a raw `connection refused` where the
classified `no mesh running at ... - run `cotal up`` sentence (and its registry prune) used to be.
The catch in `connectOrThrow` runs the preflight on the dial failure so the classified refusal is
what escapes; delete it and the raw error is the refusal again, end to end through the real binary.
THIS IS ITS OWN FIXTURE, not a fourteenth entry in attach-reconnect.json, because of the specifier
boundary that fixture's own notes describe. Every mutation there lands in
`implementations/cli/src/commands/agents.ts` and builds `@cotal-ai/cli`. This one lands in
`dist/`, and a CLI build does not rebuild that package. Measured at 40169db43 with the mutant
applied and only the CLI built: cell G stayed green and the grader reported UNGRADABLE, the
mutation applied and nothing ran it. With the workspace built first the same mutant reddened
cell G on the named line (54 passed, 18 failed against 55/17 for the same tree unmutated, the
one extra red being that line). The command here builds the workspace and the CLI, and restores
both, because `dist/` is gitignored and git cannot be the recovery for it.

mutations.name: the issuer dial's transport error escapes as the first attach's refusal
mutations.expectRed: ...saying the mesh is not there, in the CLI's own words
mutations.cell: ...saying the mesh is not there, in the CLI's own words
mutations.note: Cell G pins an instance with `--on`, so this connect is the first thing that touches the broker, and the link is severed under it. Unmutated, the preflight classifies the dead link and the CLI prints `no mesh running at`; mutated, the issuer dial's `connection refused` is what the operator reads. The other three checks in cell G (non-zero exit, a single failure mark, no reconnect banner) stay green under this mutant, so a kill here is a claim about the refusal's WORDS specifically, which is the whole finding.
